content.title: HOUSEHOLD FIXES FOR ANNOYING LITTLE AILMENTS THAT ACTUALLY WORK
facts: **Hangnail Pain** – Soak the finger in warm water with 1 tsp olive oil for 5 minutes to soften skin before trimming.
**Stuffy Nose** – Hold a warm, damp washcloth over your sinuses for 2 minutes to loosen congestion fast.
**Bug Bite Itch** – Press a warm spoon against the bite for 10 seconds; heat disrupts the itch signal to your brain.
**Toothache Throb** – Rinse with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in a cup of water) to pull down swelling around the gum.
**Leg Cramp at Night** – Gently pull your toes toward your shin and hold for 20 seconds to force the muscle to release.
**Splinter Removal** – Dab a bit of baking soda paste on it and cover overnight; the sliver often rises to the surface on its own.
**Dry Cracked Heels** – Rub a thin layer of petroleum jelly on feet, then wear socks to bed to lock in moisture overnight.
**Nosebleed** – Pinch the soft part of your nose and lean slightly forward for a full 10 minutes without checking early.

caption:
A few of these are worth keeping in your back pocket. For a stuffy nose, that warm washcloth trick works because heat helps dilate the blood vessels in your sinuses, which loosens built-up mucus so it drains instead of sitting there making you miserable. With a leg cramp, pulling your toes toward your shin forces the calf muscle into a stretch, which interrupts the involuntary contraction causing the cramp in the first place. And for a splinter, baking soda paste slightly draws fluid to the surface of the skin overnight, which helps push shallow splinters up so they're easier to grab with tweezers in the morning. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so give these a try and see what works for you.
